subject: Learning Methods
title: The Zettelkasten Method
description: A 60-second lesson on The Zettelkasten Method.

hook.text: Niklas Luhmann published 70 books and 400 articles using a box of 90,000 interlinked index cards he built over decades.

buildup.text: Each card holds one idea written in his own words. Cards link to related cards via numbered references.

discovery.text: The network of links creates emergent structure. Ideas that were captured years apart connect in unexpected.

twist.text: Zettelkasten is not about collecting. It is about dialogue with your notes. You write new cards in response to old ones.

climax.text: Write one idea per note. Link it to related notes. Over time, a web of knowledge grows that generates new insights.

punchline.text: One idea per note. Link them all. Watch the web grow.

quiz.question: What makes the Zettelkasten method unique compared to standard note-taking?
options: Notes are organized by date instead of topic
Each note links to related notes, creating an emergent network of ideas
Notes must be handwritten on index cards
